statement.p: Use cylindrical coordinates to calculate : \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} x^2+y^2\,dV\qquad \mathcal{W}: x^2+y^2\le 25 ,\quad 0\le z \le 4 \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} (x^2+y^2)\,dV=

static.solution:
\mathcal{W} onto the xy-plane is the region inside the circle {x}^2+{y}^2=25. In polar coordinates, \mathcal{D}: \,0\le \theta \le 2\pi,\,0\le r\le 5 The upper and lower boundaries are the planes z=4 and z=0, respectively.
Therefore, \mathcal{W} has the following description in cylindrical coordinates: \mathcal{W}: \,0\le \theta \le 2\pi,\,0\le r\le 5,\,0\le z\le 4 The integral in cylindrical coordinates is thus \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} ({x}^2+{y}^2) \,dV= \int_0^{2\pi } \int_0^{5} \int_0^{4} {r}^2\cdot r \,dz \,dr \,d\theta= \int_0^{2\pi } \int_0^{5} \int_0^{4} {r}^3 \,dz \,dr \,d\theta=\left(\int_0^{2\pi } 1 \,d\theta \right)\left(\int_0^{5} {r}^3 \,dr\right)\left(\int_0^{4} 1 \,dz\right)= 2\pi \cdot {4}\cdot \frac{{r}^4}{4}\bigg|_0^{5}= 2\cdot {5}^4\cdot\pi \approx 3926.99
